title: Consumer always-apply for edit-only fields
description: Proves the funnel Consumer's US-027 editOnly preservation guard: any Property marked IsEditOnly=true must preserve its user value against ingest writes regardless of batch timestamps. Unlike US-021/US-022 which only protect user state when the latest user edit is strictly newer than the ingest batch, this guard runs unconditionally for every ingest CREATE/MODIFY. The fixture covers a single Order with a editOnly notes field, a user CREATE that seeds notes='VIP', and a strictly newer ingest MODIFY that attempts to set notes='SPAM' alongside an unrelated status change.

ingestBatch.note: Strictly NEWER than userBatch so the US-021 timestamp guard alone cannot protect notes — only the US-027 editOnly guard can.

sequence: funnel.Consumer.SetEditOnlyField(fn) where fn queries repo.ListProperties and returns Property.IsEditOnly

expected.preserveEditOnlyFieldsOutcome: ingestBatch.edits[0] has its Properties rewritten: notes stripped from the ingest map and re-merged from the current bleve doc (notes='VIP'); status='shipped' and orderID='ord-1' pass through unchanged.
expected.leakGuard: notes MUST remain 'VIP' — the string 'SPAM' must NOT appear in the final bleve doc; status MUST be updated to 'shipped' to prove non-editOnly fields are still mutable by ingest.

notes: Run the integration test with `go test -tags integration ./test/integration/... -run EditOnly`. Requires Docker for testcontainers.

US-021's user-edit-wins guard is timestamp-based; it only filters ingest edits whose batch.Timestamp is older than LatestUserEditAt. US-027 is a strictly stronger guarantee for fields marked IsEditOnly=true — it runs unconditionally and never lets ingest touch those fields, even when the ingest batch is newer.

preserveEditOnlyFields runs BEFORE resolveConflicts in applyBatchWithHistory. The two passes compose: an ingest edit may be first stripped of editOnly fields, then dropped entirely by the stale-timestamp guard if the user has a newer edit on any remaining field. The edit-only guard skips DELETE edits (which are all-or-nothing and delegate to US-021).

The parity fixture intentionally uses a STRICTLY NEWER ingest timestamp so the test cannot accidentally pass via the US-021 path. Any future regression that removes the editOnly guard will surface here as notes='SPAM' in the final bleve doc.

Production main.go does NOT yet wire SetEditOnlyField against the live OMS schema — the integration test wires a local closure over repo.ListProperties. Follow-up work for the serving path should build a cached (objectType, field)->IsEditOnly lookup at startup or on ObjectType schema-change events and call SetEditOnlyField once.
